releaseNotes:
The Challenger Lab, explanations where the features are, prompts as files, and a fairer governance search. Your models, saved games and codes are not changed.

Challenger Lab (AI Lab, tab Challengers)
• Pick a market and a side. An AI is shown your two leaders on it, their formulas and where they go wrong, and writes up to 3 new models. A run costs 1 AI request.
• The phone tests each one on games the AI never saw. Four gates: it brings something new; it is judged on games that judged no challenger of that market before; it does not pick as a leader does; it beats every leader by more than luck.
• Nothing is added without your tap. A challenger you add plays a 30-game trial before it votes in All-Star or counts in governance.
• From AI Chat: "run the Challenger Lab on away total".

Training
• A run also fits the four half formulas to the points by half, and keeps a fit only when the held-out games are clearly closer.

Governance
• A model's sides count only in games played after its formulas were last saved; the page lists the models counted on fewer games.
• Patterns can carry one condition: one side, a high or a low line, 60% or more stated, early or late in the season.
• The four half markets are searched too.
• "Ask an AI for pattern ideas": copy a prompt, paste the answer, and the phone counts each idea by the same bar. The app sends nothing itself.
• Expect the watched patterns to change. A true pattern is found somewhat later than before; that is the price.

Prompts as a file
• Under every "Copy prompt" button: Save .md, Save .txt and Share file.

Question marks and the Guide
• A small question mark beside a switch or a choice opens a few plain sentences. The Guide holds them all, with a search; it opens from the top of every page and from Settings.
• Team aliases have a screen of their own.

Records
• A winner pick on a side the bookmaker showed no price for is no longer counted. Before, it counted as a win at a made-up price of 1.909. This lowers the winner record of models with such games; the record says how many picks were left out. Tell me if you want the old counting back.
• Every record line in AI Chat names what it counts.

AI Chat
• The game scan and the lines tool know home total, away total, the half markets and mixed markets such as "Winner and total".
• A booking code of another sport can be inspected without loading it. Ten cards over many games can be read page by page.
• The chat export says per tool how long it waited and worked.
• When the AI spends its whole reply thinking, the app asks it once for the answer. Before, you read its planning and had to ask again.
• Minting: the card and the AI give the odds at the prices just read, and the deadline with its date.
• The bookmaker's list is not read again for the same Betslip within 3 minutes.

Not in this version
• Question marks on Slips and stakes, AI Chat settings and Results.

Fixes for AI Chat and one for LINE+. Your models, saved games and codes are not changed.

Tables in AI Chat
• A table the AI writes itself is now drawn as a table: names on top, a line, the rows in columns, and it scrolls sideways when it is wide. Before, you saw the bars and dashes it was typed with. This is what made NVIDIA's answers hard to read.
• "Show the weekly report" now shows the report. Before, the answer could come out empty, because the report is words and the chat only knew how to show rows.
• When the AI reads a kept result again it gets the whole text. Before, it got the first 400 letters, cut in the middle of a number, which is how a 602-472 became 602-473.
• Column names sent to the AI are set apart clearly. Two calls failed in your chat because three names ran together. The column "by, on average" is now "average margin".
• A line of dashes is drawn as a thin line, and *single stars* slant the words.

Speed
• Checking the Betslip no longer works the models' whole record out again when only prices of games not yet played have changed. In your chat that was 29 to 45 seconds of every check. The record is still worked out again when a game finishes, a score is corrected or a model changes.

The app started anew after an export
• The cause is not found. Nothing in the export ends the app, and your export file was written whole. Either Android closed the app while another app was in front, or it crashed.
• From now on every chat export says why the app last stopped, in words, as Android recorded it. If it happens again, export a chat and send it: it will say which of the two it was.
• The long work on the record (above) may have been running at that moment, and Android closes a busy app in the background sooner. That work is gone now, which may be enough. This is a guess, not a finding.

LINE+
• LINE+ stood at 102 won, 0 lost, 100% although it was never trained. On games where the bookmaker showed no price for the winner, the app took the favourite of the bookmaker's own handicap as LINE+'s pick. That is no longer a pick. Untrained, LINE+ has no record.

Good to know
• The speed gain and the LINE+ cause were found by rebuilding the cases in tests, not by measuring on your phone. The "Took" line of a Betslip check will show it: "the record" should be about a second.
• Still open: for every model, a winner pick on a game without a winner price is counted at the stand-in price of 1.909. Not changed here, because it changes every model's record.

This version finishes what 2.24.0 left open and adds the honest board to AI Chat. 2.24.0 was never published on its own, so its notes are below these and both arrive together. Your models, saved games and codes are not changed.

Cards and the price rule
• A model's own strength filter now runs before the price rule, so a weak pick is not offered just because it is the only one that pays.
• An empty card says why in one sentence, and the reasons are under "Measured chances".
• Half-game picks and winner-and-total picks are judged by the price rule too.
• All-Star's card stops when its time is up instead of working on.

Models page
• Weekly report: what changed in the roles, who leads each market, what needs more games.
• "What the words mean": the 18 words the app uses for evidence, each in one line.
• A model's own page lists its roles.

Governance page
• Each watched pattern shows its record so far and how many more games it needs, as it stands, before it can be told from luck. Where more games would not help, it says that instead.

AI Chat
• "Which model is best at away totals?" is answered from the honest board: each model on the games since its formulas were saved, at the prices taken. Under 50 bets a record never leads.
• New answers: a model's strengths, the roles, All-Star's four rules side by side, the weekly report, and a governance report (how many patterns were measured, each beside the plain rule of always taking that side, and what the watched ones still need).
• The chat names a code's chance and suggested stake in the words of the Codes tab, and can remove from the Betslip the picks that do not pay.
• Asking for the slate twice within three minutes does not read the bookmaker's list again.

Notices (only from background checks, once each)
• A role was switched by the weekly review. The weekly report is ready. No closing line was read on a day.

Backup
• Roles and stakes settings are in the safety copy. A restored copy gives the same honest board; this is tested on your recorded games.

Good to know
• None of this was tried on a phone. The numbers are checked by tests; the new screens and the chat wiring are checked only by the build.
• The governance search itself is unchanged. Born-on sides, new search conditions and the half markets as markets of their own are not in it: each changes what governance finds and needs its own study first.
• The Challenger Lab is not in this version. Only its gates are written and tested: a copy of a parent is refused, a winner on practice games only is refused, held-out games are not used twice. There is no screen and no AI run yet.
• Pausing a model still writes every saved game once.
• In the chat's record tool a market is now named in words ("away total"), not in a field of its own.

This version changes what the cards offer. A pick is now offered only where its measured chance pays at the bookmaker's price, so cards are shorter and some are empty. An empty card is an answer: nothing paid today. One switch brings back the cards of 2.23. Your models, saved games and codes are not changed.

The price rule (Decisions and Models tabs, card "Price rule")
• Under each pick: its measured chance, the price, and whether it pays. Under each card: how many picks were not offered, each with its reason.
• Each model has a role per market and direction: on, or watching. A watching model still makes its pick and the pick is still counted; it is only not offered. Roles are reviewed once a week from the record; you can switch one on by hand.
• The switch at the top turns the rule off.

All-Star
• One vote per voice: near-copies of a model speak once, and "5 of 8" counts voices and names who is against.
• All-Star takes the market that pays best and abstains, with the reason, when the voices are split or no line pays.
• It starts on match totals and winner only. Team totals, handicap and halves are watching until its own record allows them.
• You choose which rule the card shows: the new one, the rule of 2.23, all voices agree, or the market's leader. All four are written down before tip-off and counted side by side on the Governance compare page.

Codes tab: "Slips and stakes"
• An open code shows the chance that all its games win, what that is worth at its odds, the size that keeps the chance at your floor (20% to start), and how your finished codes of that size did.
• Your codes beside the same picks staked one by one.
• Optional: a suggested stake (flat, or a share of your balance with a cap), a daily stop, the bookmaker's bonus, and a balance log. The app places no bet.

AI Chat
• "Check my Betslip" is answered about your own picks: models on each side, by how many points, and All-Star's pick.
• Every card pick has an id (P12); "load exactly these" adds by id. Ten cards fit one answer up to about 17 games.
• An instruction may be 500 characters (it was cut at 140 without notice). Write the cut ones again in full.
• The export holds your instructions, the app's rules and how long each tool took.

Good to know
• None of this was tried on a phone. The numbers were checked by tests on a recorded board.
• A chance is "measured" from finished games. Until enough have finished, cards are built as in 2.23 and codes show no chance.
• All-Star's card takes longer to build (not measured), because the old rule is still worked out beside the new one.
• Two picks of one game in a code move together; the code's chance is then marked rough.
• Not in this version: a model's own strength filter moved before the price rule, stakes in AI Chat, roles on the scoreboard card. They come with 2.25.0.

This version is about waiting. The assistant made you wait far too long, and the chat you sent on 22 November shows why: of 464 seconds, the AI model itself took 20. The app took the rest. Your models, saved games and codes are not changed, and no model's pick is different.

Faster
• The cards of the Betslip (every model's picks, All-Star, the high-agreement filter) are worked out about six times faster the first time and about nine times faster when the assistant asks for cards the app has already worked out. The app used to read each game's whole board again for every pick of every model, and asked every model about every game up to four times. It now does each of these once and keeps the answer.
• After the assistant pauses a model, loads a code or changes anything else, its answer is shown and the chat is free at once. It used to stay busy until every page of the app had been filled again.
• After such a change the app used to write every saved game to its database again and work out your record from them again, also when nothing about a game had changed. A saved game that did not change is now left alone.
• Picks written in words ("Duke over 148.5") are looked up six at a time instead of one after the other.
• When you ask for one card (All-Star only, or one model), only that is built.

Fixed
• "Cincinnati Bearcats under 91.5", a team's own total, was put on the match total Under 143.5 and reported as found. A total written in words is now moved to a line the bookmaker offers by 6 points at most. A number far from the match total is taken as that team's own total if the bookmaker has the line, and the assistant is told so. Otherwise the pick is refused and the assistant is told which lines are offered.
• "Texas Longhorns under 92.5" was put on a later game of Texas than the one on the Betslip. When a team has two games coming up, the game on the Betslip is taken; without one, the game that tips off first. Writing both teams ("Texas v Ohio State under 140.5") still decides it.

New in the chat export
• Pulling today's games, building cards and adding picks in words now say how long each part took: reading the bookmaker, the models, saving. If something is still slow, export the chat and send it; it will show which part.

Good to know
• Reading the bookmaker is not faster. Pulling today's games still reads the list and every game's board, and on a slow connection that is most of that wait.
• Pausing a model still makes the app write every saved game once, because each saved game holds only the results of the models that are on. The working out is faster; the writing is as before.
• The speed was measured on a computer, not on a phone. How much faster your phone feels is not known until you try it.

The assistant can now book matches of any sport the bookmaker offers, not only NCAA men's games. Your models, saved games and codes are not changed.

Booking other sports
• Paste your list in the chat and say "book this". Write each match as "Home v Away" with the pick on the next line and an empty line between matches, as in the list of 22 November.
• The assistant looks each match up at the bookmaker, finds the pick and shows you a card before anything is made: how many matches were found, the combined odds, every match with its pick and price, and every match it could not book with the reason. The code is made only after you tap Confirm.
• Sports: football, basketball, tennis, ice hockey, handball, volleyball, baseball, American football, rugby, cricket, table tennis, darts, badminton and MMA. Football is searched first. Name the sport in your message if the whole list is one sport; it is faster.
• Picks it reads: Home, Away, Draw; "1UP" and "2UP"; "Home or Draw", "Draw or Away", "Home or Away"; Over and Under on the match and on one team (write the team on the next line); both teams to score (Yes or No); Draw No Bet; Win to Nil and Clean Sheet with Yes or No; handicaps; odd or even.
• Up to 50 matches in one code. Matches up to 14 days ahead are searched.
• A match that is not on the bookmaker's upcoming list, has already started, or does not offer the pick is left out and named, with the reason. Nothing is replaced by a similar pick.
• The code is saved in Codes with the label "Other sports". Codes has a new filter with that name. Nothing goes on the Betslip.

What the app does not do with other sports
• No model, no stats, no opinion. The app books what you wrote. It does not say whether a pick is good, and these codes are not scored in Results.

Fixed
• "Book this" with a list of football matches was answered with "the app only covers NCAA men's basketball". The assistant now gets the booking tool for such a message and is told never to refuse a booking because of the sport.
• Picks written in words ("Duke over 148.5"): every pick that was found and added to the Betslip was also reported to the assistant as not found, so it could tell you a pick had failed when it was on the Betslip. Fixed.
• Adding picks written in words was stopped after 60 seconds on a slow day with nothing added. It now gets 180 seconds.

Good to know
• Team names must be close to the bookmaker's. "Hertha" finds "Hertha BSC"; a nickname the bookmaker does not use may not be found, and the card says so.
• If the bookmaker limits requests, the assistant tells you and you can try again after a short while.
• This version was checked with recorded answers of the bookmaker. It has not been tried on a phone yet.

New inputs for formulas, taken from the team game log, and two yardsticks to measure every model against. Your models, versions and saved games are not changed: a model that does not use the new inputs gives exactly the numbers it gave before.

New inputs for formulas (37)
• Recent form: points for and against over a team's last 3, 5 and 10 games (for example home.l5_pts, away.l10_opp).
• Rest and load: days since the last game, games in the last 7 days.
• The app's own ratings from the log: attack, defence, strength of opponents, and what the home court has been worth this season.
• Halves: points for and against in each half, and the share of points scored in the first half.
• Last season as a whole: points for and against and the two ratings. Given only once all of last season has been read.
• The bookmaker's own lines: match total, team totals, handicap, the half lines, and its chances with its margin taken out.
• Every value is the one that stood before tip-off. If a value cannot be known (a team has not yet played 5 games, the log has no such date), the formula gives no number for that game. Nothing is guessed.
• The inputs can be used in the formulas of a market. Decision and Pick Gate formulas cannot use them.
• In the formula editor they are under "Game values". All prompts for an outside AI list them with their meaning.

After updating
• In Settings, "Team game log", tap "Fill this and last season now" once (about a minute). Until then the form inputs have no values and a model that uses them shows "NO DATA".

Frozen with the game
• The values a game was worked out with are saved with it and in its capture receipt, so a result is always judged on what was known before tip-off. A game saved before this version gets its values from the log by the date of the game.

LINE and LINE+
• LINE is the bookmaker's line on every market. It never picks. It is shown beside your models so that you see what "no opinion" scores.
• LINE+ starts as the line. "Train" fits four numbers on this phone: recent form on the totals and the app's ratings on the margin. No AI is asked. If your model cannot beat LINE+, it adds little to the line.
• Neither has a vote in All-Star. Neither can be edited or deleted; LINE cannot be trained.
• For every model: on a market where its number is exactly the bookmaker's line, it makes no pick, and the game counts neither as won nor as lost for it there.

Which inputs matter
• "Show what the log holds" lists, per market, the inputs that would have brought the line closer to the result on games they were not fitted on. It needs about 90 finished saved games with a board. Out of many inputs a few look good by luck, so read it as a hint.

Not in this version
• Whether a coming game is on a neutral court: the app cannot know it before tip-off.
• The price rule deciding what the models, All-Star and slips offer; All-Star on the new rules; stakes; the Challenger Lab.

Fix release for the AI chat and for the prompts that build models. Nothing you saved is changed; no model, version or receipt changes.

Model prompts (Models, "Ask External AI to Build Model")
• Every prompt now lists all 10 markets the app plays: 5 full-game formulas, 4 half formulas, and Winner and Total, which needs no formula of its own. Until now the prompts said "5 markets" and left the halves to a later question, so an outside AI built five and stopped.
• One box for each half market (1st-half O/U, 1st-half Handicap, 2nd-half O/U, 2nd-half Handicap), all ticked for a new model. An unticked half is left out of the prompt.
• An upgrade prompt says for each model which of the 10 markets it plays and which it does not, and asks which to fill.

Betslip in the chat
• A pick the bookmaker does not offer is no longer added. The answer names the lines that are offered.
• "Remove Missouri" works: a pick is removed by team name or in words. If nothing matches, the answer lists what is on the Betslip.
• "Check my Betslip" reads your own picks, quickly. Before, it answered with the models' picks for those games.
• Picks in words also find tomorrow's games.
• Before a code is made, a pick that the last reading does not show is read again. Picks are named in words ("Under 172.5"), not by numbers.
• A change to the Betslip no longer waits for the models' cards.

Understanding you
• "+25" and "25+" mean 25 or more. The AI adds no upper limit of its own.
• A range you set is never widened. An empty search names the nearest lines and asks.
• Handicap: a plus is the team that gets points. With no sign and no side named, the AI asks first. A search shows both sides of each line.
• An answer names a game by its teams.
• The chat knows all 10 markets.

Waiting and stops
• A code is shown by its picks at once. The models' view of it comes only when asked.
• Diagnosing one model does the work of that model only (before: every model, twice), and it can be stopped.
• After Stop, your next message is answered for itself. Before, it was answered with a report on the stopped job.

Models on and off
• Several models, a tier, or "all except" go on one card. A model already in that state is listed, not reported as failed. The answer shows which models are on now.

Also
• A kept table is read when a column is named slightly differently, and the answer lists the columns.
• Combined odds are shown with two decimals.

Not in this version
• The rest of the list from the three chats of 20 November: Winner and Total in the search, the two slow local reads, and the price and chance items. New formula inputs from the team game log, the yardstick models, last season's table.

New: measured chances, a price rule, and a team game log. This version also holds free picks. Nothing you saved is changed; no model, version or receipt changes.

Free picks (AI Lab, third tab)
• Each model takes, from every open option of a game's whole board, the one with the most value by its own numbers. The notes of 2.20.0 below describe the tab; that version was never published on its own, and this one holds it.
• New here: Codes has a "Free picks" filter.

Measured chances
• Until now a chance took the whole gap between a model's number and the bookmaker's line as true. The app now measures, on your finished saved games, how much of such a gap showed in the results: per market, apart for Over and Under, home and away side. The spread is measured too.
• A model with under 50 results in a market uses the figure of all models together; with more, its own is mixed in. Under 50 games there is no measured chance and the stated one stands.
• Forward only: a game is never judged with itself or a later game.
• Scoreboard card ("What it is good at…"): the share of the gap that holds up with its range, and a chart of stated, measured and came true.
• A game's page: under each model's options, "Measured 54%, could be as low as 50% (stated 63%)".

The price rule
• A pick is offered only when measured chance times price is above 1 by a margin, and the margin grows when the chance is known only roughly. Every verdict says why: "55% at 1.70 does not pay: break-even is 59%."
• Free picks: once chances are measured, each model makes a second pick on them. Pick of the day and the code then come from the picks the rule offered, and a day may have none. Refused picks are kept and scored: "The price rule refused 40 picks; they went 18–22."
• Scoreboard card: what the rule would have done with each model's own first picks, each judged from the games before it.
• The models' own picks, All-Star, slips and governance still pick as before. The rule is shown beside them, not yet applied.

Team game log (Settings, "Team game log")
• Every finished game of the season from the ESPN scoreboard: opponent, home, away or neutral court, points, points by half, overtime, conference and tournament marks.
• From it: the app's own attack and defence ratings corrected for opponents, the measured home-court value, form and rest, each as it stood before a game.
• Filled a few days at a time while the app is open, or at once with "Fill the whole season now". The page lists what is missing.
• No formula reads the log yet.

Not in this version
• New formula inputs from the log, the yardstick models LINE and LINE+, last season's table, roles per market, All-Star on the new rules, stakes, the Challenger Lab.

New: Free picks. Each model looks at every open option on a game's whole board and takes what it likes most: any market, any line, any price. Nothing you saved is changed, and no model, version or receipt changes.

Where
• AI Lab, third tab: "Free picks".

How a pick is made
• From the model's own numbers the app works out its chance for every outcome that is settled by the score: all 24 markets of the board (totals, team totals, handicaps, the halves, winner and total, 1X2, draw no bet, three-way handicap, half time/full time, exact total, odd/even, overtime).
• The model takes the option with the most value: its chance times the price, less one. If nothing has value above zero it takes nothing.
• One pick per model and game, at the price of that moment. It is never changed afterwards.
• Picks are made when you open the tab or tap "Look again now". The app asks no server for it: it uses the boards it has already read. A game whose whole board was never read gets no pick; the tab says how many there are. Boards are stored only while "New markets" is on.

What the tab shows
• Per model: its open picks with the price, its chance, the bookmaker's chance and the break-even; its pick of the day; its long shot of the day (5.00 and more); a code of its own (three games at most) that you can make at the bookmaker, shown beside the same picks as singles.
• "Chosen freely by several models", with a record of its own.
• A record by price band (under 1.50 up to above 10.00): won, lost, return, what the model said against what came true, and beside it what every option of that band returned on the same games. It also says how many more settled picks are needed before a return can be told from luck.
• A band that is losing by more than luck explains gets a notice. You can switch a band off for a model. The app switches nothing off by itself.
• A free-pick formula per model, which you can edit. The starting formula is the value alone.

Please know
• The chances are stated, not measured. A free chooser goes where the model disagrees most with the bookmaker, and that is often where the model is most wrong. Treat the record by price band as the test.
• Long prices take long to judge: about 400 settled picks at 2.00 and about 3,600 at 10.00.
• A model without half formulas is offered no half market.
• The record of free picks is on this tab only. It is not counted on model cards, the scoreboard or All-Star, and All-Star's own picks are exactly as before.
• A deleted game takes its free picks with it.

AI Chat
• New tool free_picks_read: ask "what would KP take freely?" or "pick of the day".

Not in this version
• Measured chances, the team game log, the new price rule, All-Star on the new rules, stakes, the Challenger Lab.
